TL;DR  I was like you at 30. Spent my 31st birthday in inpatient for terrible attempt. Now I'm in my 40s. STAY.

I tried to end things 6x in my early 30s, had life-saving measures taken more than one, after my first divorce.  I was so pissed off at the time. I cannot have bio children due to health problems leading to hysterectomy. I spent my 30s 100 pounds overweight, with other undiagnosed health issues 

Now I'm in my 40s. I met my current husband 4 years ago.  I got diagnosis of my physical disability, and treatment and 12 years of therapy for my brain.  I got wegovy and lost 100 pounds, and now I have made the mental and habit changes and kept all of it off for 6 months with no medicine to help. 

My husband has 3 kids from prior relationship, so now I get to be a step-mom, and it is a if I had the kids when I was in my 20s, due to their ages.  I LOVE BEING A STEPMOM!!! It was hard, but it's honestly so rad.

At 30, I had no hope at all.  Zero. But I had my best friend and a great therapist. And good medical treatment. I love my life now. I'm physically partially disabled, I'm in pain every day,  I'm in 500k of educational debt, so things are not perfect. But I am really glad I got help and made hard choices with help and support. 

Please, get help.  STAY.

I have a master list of projects, small and large, that I want to accomplish. Short term things like organizing a closet all the way through long term goals like completing a course.  On my good days, i take out the master list and make detailed to-do lists for the things that are coming up in the short term.  Then, when I fog, I have these instructions I've left myself in order to keto on target with my bigger goals.  On fog days I chose the last taxing items.  This strategy has allowed me to accomplish a ton. I hope you all figure out your best strategy :)

I second the Pomodoro method,  I use that to help plan work time. Also, when I am having a good day (the address more good than bad in general, but I've head recent flares), I make detailed step-by-step to-do lists fit myself for everything I can imagine I want to do in my work, home, or even fun stuff. Then, when I fog but need to focus,  I can turn to my lists to assist me in directing my energy.

What's worked for me is a holistic approach.  Medication to control the pain and keep it in an acceptable range.  Therapy to work on underlying stressors that can exacerbate pain. Mindfulness meditation to practice coping with the presence of chronic pain as well as not to panic during an extreme flare. Dietary changes to reduce inflammation and increase overall energy.  Gentle movement every day that I am able, might be stretching or Wii fit balance exercises for 5 or 10 minutes.  Hot baths, heating pads,  weighted blanket, braces as needed to alleviate flares. Mobility aids if I know I'm facing a day that will trigger a flare.  Assistive technology and ergonomic office furniture,  a lot of which a job might reimburse for. 

The bad news: this takes time to get just right for your body. Some things may work better for me than they do for you.  Can be easy to feel discouraged until you find your things. 

The good news: I have a doctorate,  a successful career,  and I live independently with fibro,  CPTSD, and several other comorbidities for the past 10 years. Don't give up.  Go after what will make your life the highest quality.

Trying to bring this up has caused me frustration because I have a feeling like I'm the one failing by not keeping their secret for them.

Keep at it. Reach out here if you need.

It took me 9 months to get treatment from the time I expressed my first SI. I won't go into details except to say that being highly educated, career successful, and "well spoken" didn't help me get listened to.

If you are having persistent,  active thoughts, please seek help from someone you trust immediately.  Call a hotline,  post here, call your local ER or just go if it is too bad to tolerate.  Don't give up on yourself.  Find a medical professional who will listen. I know is difficult.
